title: Durable In-Memory Key-Value Store
prompt:
Build a durable, single-process key-value store. Keys are strings and values may be any JSON-serializable value. Use UTF-8 JSON Lines so each record occupies one newline-terminated line.

### Part 1 — Log-backed recovery

Implement `LogBackedKVStore(path)` with `set(key, value)`, `get(key, default=None)`, and `delete(key)`. Every mutation must append one record, flush it, and call `os.fsync` before changing the visible in-memory state. Reconstruct state by replaying the log in constructor order. A delete of a missing key is still a durable no-op record. Accept a malformed final fragment only when the file does not end in a newline, modeling a torn last write; malformed complete records must raise `ValueError`. Reject non-string keys and values that cannot be serialized as JSON.

### Part 2 — Multi-file snapshots

Implement `MultiFileSnapshotKVStore(root, max_file_bytes=1024)` with the same in-memory `set`, `get`, and `delete` behavior plus `save_snapshot()` and `load_snapshot()`. `save_snapshot()` writes sorted key/value records into a new generation directory, never splits a record across files, calls `fsync` for every data file, and atomically publishes the generation name through a `CURRENT` manifest. Return that generation name. Every non-empty data file must be at most `max_file_bytes`; if one encoded record is too large, raise `ValueError` without replacing the previously published snapshot. `load_snapshot()` replaces memory with the generation named by `CURRENT`, or with an empty mapping when no manifest exists. Ignore unpublished generation directories.

example.reasoning: Constructor replay rebuilds the in-memory mapping from durable mutation records.
